name: Amariah
overview: Amariah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known for his role in distributing portions to his brothers. His service and responsibilities are noted within the Levitical duties, emphasizing his active participation in the priestly and tribal functions. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Amariah means 'YHWH has said,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord's authority and declaration. This proper name is recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:15 and highlights the spiritual significance carried by his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Amariah as a son of Levi, linking him directly to the Levitical lineage. Beyond this paternal relationship, no further family connections are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Amariah's significance lies in his Levitical service, specifically in the distribution of portions to his brothers, which underscores the organized and faithful administration of tribal duties under God's covenant. His role exemplifies the faithful stewardship expected of the Levites in supporting the worship and communal life of Israel, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:15.
